reason: E1 shows that isothermal exposure at 800°C forms Cr2O3 and spinel oxides and enhances wear resistance, supporting the first two premises. However, no cited evidence addresses thermal cycling, its effect on oxide formation/healing, or the oxide's role as a solid lubricant and diffusion barrier, leaving the remaining premises unsupported.
premises: Thermal exposure of FeNiCrCoCu coatings at 800°C forms a protective Cr2O3 and spinel oxide layer
This oxide layer enhances wear resistance
Thermal cycling accelerates formation and healing of the oxide layer
The oxide layer acts as a diffusion barrier and solid lubricant
The oxide layer remains adherent during wear
